result.summary: The layout is mostly coherent, but there is a clearly broken text overlap in the 'Popular right now' card metadata, plus a few smaller consistency issues with the favorite buttons and truncated carousel items.

issues.description: Under 'Tokumaru Ramen Bar' the metadata line renders two overlapping strings: '25–35 min' and '€0 delivery' are drawn on top of each other ('25–3 5 Ordelivery'), making the text unreadable.
issues.suggestion: Render the metadata as a single flex row with proper spacing/separators instead of absolutely positioned or stacked labels; ensure the delivery time and delivery fee are separate nodes with a gap and '·' divider.

issues.description: Favorite (heart) buttons are styled inconsistently between the two 'Popular right now' cards — the first has a white circular background with a dark outline heart, the second has a dark/transparent background with a white heart.
issues.suggestion: Use one shared favorite-button component with a consistent background scrim and icon color across all cards.

issues.description: The third item in 'Fastest near you' ('Trattoria Piccol…') is clipped at the right screen edge with its title cut mid-word and no visible affordance that the row scrolls.
issues.suggestion: Add horizontal padding/peek so the next card is partially visible with a clear cut, truncate titles with an ellipsis, and add a scroll indicator or snap behavior.

issues.description: The second 'Popular right now' card (pizza, −20%) is abruptly cut by the bottom navigation bar with no bottom safe-area padding, so the card appears to slide under the tab bar without a shadow or fade.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom content inset equal to the tab bar height and a subtle scroll edge fade/elevation on the nav bar.

issues.description: Category chips row is clipped at the right edge (a partial chip is visible), and the promo banner's 'Order now' button plus icon-only buttons (notification bell, hearts) rely on visuals alone without visible labels.
issues.suggestion: Ensure icon-only controls have accessible labels/content descriptions and give the chip row edge padding so partially visible chips are obviously scrollable.
